title: Adaptive Pareto kernel router for speculative decode with bounded rollback budget
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement an adaptive runtime router that selects speculative decode destinations by optimizing a Pareto frontier between kernel-level cost (GPU time / memory pressure) and expected acceptance probability. The router enforces a bounded rollback budget (safety quota) per customer/instance to limit the operational impact of mis-routed speculative attempts. Goal: lower average per-token cost and maintain P95 latency and model output quality by routing low-risk requests aggressively while keeping strict safety caps for high-uncertainty traffic.
background_and_motivation: We currently run conservative speculative decode routing which limits cost savings. Operators have requested a more aggressive cost-aware router that still provides strong guarantees on rollback exposure and latency SLOs. Rather than static priority lists, using an empirical Pareto frontier computed from kernel signatures, sequence-length distribution, and historic acceptance metrics should let the runtime prefer low-cost, high-accept proposals while capping potential fallout when acceptance is uncertain.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end P95 latency for served requests does not regress by more than 5% on canonical benchmark traffic
Overall rollback rate <= 2% per customer under steady-state synthetic load
Per-token average cost decreases by >= 8% on agent-simulated workloads compared to baseline routing
No drop in evaluated output quality (ROUGE / BLEU / task-specific eval) beyond noise band on our prompt corpus
design_notes: Router computes a running Pareto frontier of candidate kernel/model variants using features: kernel-cost-estimate (ms per token), measured acceptance probability for a small prefill probe, kv-cache affinity, and model-compatibility signatures. Routing decision is a two-step process: (1) shortlist candidates that lie near the cost/acceptance Pareto front given the request context; (2) apply safety quotas (rollback tokens remaining, customer SLA tier, and regional capacity) to pick the final speculative target. Safety quota state is maintained per-customer with a leaky-bucket decrement on each speculative fallback. Configurable knobs: quota window, minimum acceptance threshold, and conservative multiplier for noisy traffic classes.
implementation_plan: Prototype Pareto calculator in simulation harness using historical telemetry (2 weeks)
Add lightweight kernel-cost estimator API to runtime (1 week)
Integrate candidate shortlist logic into router decision path behind feature flag (2 weeks)
Implement per-customer rollback quota store (redis-backed) and enforcement middleware (1 week)
End-to-end integration tests and long-running soak with synthetic traffic (1 week)
Canary rollout, observe, tweak thresholds (2 weeks)
Gradual ramp to 100% with automated rollback if safety metrics exceed thresholds
rollout_plan: Deploy behind "feature-parato-router" flag. Start with internal canary (10% internal traffic) for 48h. Expand to low-risk customers (SaaS-dev tier) for 1 week. Observe rollback budget burn per-customer and per-region. If rollback rate or latency regressions exceed alerts for 30m, auto-revert flag and kill speculative dispatch. After 2 weeks of stable metrics, increase customer cohort and reduce conservative multipliers incrementally.
testing_strategy: Unit tests for Pareto candidate selection, integration tests with runtime kernel estimator, fault-injection tests to simulate mis-acceptance, and A/B experiments measuring cost and quality on held-out prompt sets. Add golden model checkpoints to ensure deterministic acceptance behavior in CI. Run long-running soak (72h) with representative production traces in staging.
risks_and_mitigations: Mis-estimated acceptance leads to higher rollback — mitigate via strict initial quotas and real-time monitoring with auto-revert
Kernel-cost estimator drift as hardware ages — mitigate by regular calibration jobs and fallback to conservative cost defaults
Customer-visible latency spikes when rollback bursts occur — mitigate with per-customer circuit-breaker and region-level throttles
Increased operational complexity — mitigate by providing clear dashboard views and a small set of tunable parameters
open_questions: What should default quota window and budget be for free-tier vs enterprise-tier customers?
How frequently should the Pareto frontier be recomputed in high-variance workloads?
Do we expose controls to customers (e.g., opt-out or custom quota) via console?
